# 2026-11-10: Nearby in Food (TR-032, plan 13)

Branch `feature/nearby`, from `feature/move-in-rules`. Merged as pull request 33 (merge `9f11a20`), reaching `main` with PR 24.

## Problem

From the walkthrough (F-11; [plan 13](../plan/13-nearby.md)): Food's Nearby could never work. No restaurant had
coordinates, because the composer collects only an address, so every distance was unknown. The walkthrough hid the
chip until a distance existed, which was never.

The owner decided in chat: geocode the restaurant addresses, and ask for the phone's location only when Nearby is
tapped.

## Cause

Nothing turned an address into coordinates. The server could compute a distance from the user's saved location, but
only for restaurants that had coordinates, and none did.

## Change

- **Backend (`food`):**
  - `GeocodingService` (new) asks Nominatim (`format=jsonv2&limit=1`) with the street, city, state and country only.
    - Requests are queued at least 1.1 s apart, with a User-Agent naming the app (`Comlinkr/1.0 (+https://comlinkr.com)`),
      a 10 s timeout and an in-memory cache.
    - Results: found, not found, or unavailable.
    - Off when `NODE_ENV=test` or `GEOCODING_ENABLED=false`.
  - `FoodGeocodeCron` (new) runs every minute and takes four restaurants (Nominatim's limit for scheduled scripts) with no coordinates and no
    `geocodeTriedAt`.
    - Found: it stores the latitude and longitude.
    - Not found: it sets only `geocodeTriedAt`, so the address is not sent again.
    - Unavailable (network, rate limit): it stops, and the next run tries again.
    - The update applies only if the address is still the one that was sent.
  - Migration `20261110180000_restaurant_geocode_tried_at` adds `Restaurant.geocodeTriedAt`.
  - `updateRestaurant`: changing the address, city, state or country without coordinates clears the coordinates and
    `geocodeTriedAt`, so the new address is geocoded.
- **App:**
  - `detectLocation.ts`: `currentPosition()` reads one position (permission first; the development location in
    `__DEV__`). `detectLocation` now uses it.
  - `foodShared.tsx`: `hasCoordinates`, `milesBetween` (haversine) and `NEARBY_MILES = 3`.
  - Food tab:
    - The Nearby chip shows when any restaurant has coordinates.
    - Tapping it reads the position, then filters to 3 miles, nearest first.
    - The distances are computed on the phone, and the position is not sent.
    - Cards show "x.x mi" once the distance is known.
    - Refused, blocked (with "Open settings"), location off and no fix each get a dialog, and the list stays where it
      was.
    - The list loads 20 at a time. While Nearby is on, further pages load, up to 200 restaurants, and the empty
      state waits for them.
    - "Locations © OpenStreetMap contributors" under the list, linking to OpenStreetMap's copyright page.
    - The empty state is "Nothing within 3 miles".
  - Sharing a restaurant no longer says "x mi away".

## How it was checked

- **Backend:** `tsc`, lint on the changed files, unit tests 123, e2e tests 62.
  - The new `test/unit/geocoding.spec.ts` covers:
    - the request carries only the address and the User-Agent;
    - two requests are at least a second apart;
    - a repeated address comes from the cache;
    - not found and unavailable;
    - the geocoder is off in tests;
    - the cron stores coordinates, marks a not-found address, and stops on an unavailable geocoder.
- **Mobile:** `pnpm typecheck`.
- **Locally:** with the backend running, the cron geocoded the 12 Los Angeles restaurants in two runs. The very first
  request timed out (10 s) and was retried on the next run, as designed. The Testville test restaurant was marked
  tried, with no coordinates. A manual request with curl to the same URL and User-Agent returned 200.
- **Address change**, through the local API as `uit_diego4`:
  - changing "211 Olympic Blvd" to "1000 Olympic Blvd" cleared the coordinates, and the next run geocoded the new
    address;
  - the old address was then put back, and came back with its original coordinates.
- **Phone** (OnePlus, Expo Go, local backend), with the development location in downtown Los Angeles:
  - after a refresh, the Nearby chip appeared; before Nearby was tapped, the cards showed no distance;
  - Nearby listed the four Olympic Blvd restaurants, each 1.1 mi away;
  - All then showed every card's distance (1.1, 5.3, 5.5, 10.7 mi).
  - With Metro restarted on a Long Beach location, every card showed 18.9 to 24.2 mi, and Nearby showed "Nothing
    within 3 miles". Metro was then put back on Los Angeles.
  - At size: 25 temporary restaurants (`uit_far`, 14 mi away, newest) pushed the four nearby ones to page 2. Nearby
    requested page 2 by itself and listed the same four, with no far one and the attribution line under them. The 25
    rows were deleted afterwards.
  - The cron ran ten a minute during the first local runs (12 requests); it was cut to four after reading the policy.

## Not checked

- **The permission prompt on the first tap and the refused or blocked dialogs.** Expo Go already held the location
  permission from the plan 08 walk, and resetting it means changing the phone's settings.
- **iOS.**
- **A real GPS reading.** The development location stands in for it.

## Notes

- The production backend will start geocoding every restaurant without coordinates once deployed, four a minute.
  Set `GEOCODING_ENABLED=false` (and restart) to stop it; Nominatim's policy requires that it can be switched off
  without a software update.
- The 1.1 s spacing and the cache are per process. Production runs one PM2 process; a second instance would double
  the rate.
- Nominatim's public service is meant for light use. If the number of restaurants grows a lot, a paid geocoder or a
  self-hosted Nominatim would be needed.
